chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'The gallina (chicken) that is gallala (fattened on feed) — its meat is not eaten until it has been fed for three days; the duck that is gallala — five days; the sheep that is gallala — ten days; the cow that is gallala — twenty days; and the camel that is gallala — forty days.'

key_terms.الْجَلَّالَةُ: Fattened on feed (specifically implying prior impurity or need for purification)

ai.seo_question: What are the waiting periods for different animals to become halal if they are fattened on feed?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the chain of al-Sakuni from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), details the specific waiting periods for 'gallala' animals to purge impurities from their meat, a ruling derived from the Prophet (PBUH) and transmitted by Imam Ali (AS). In Shia fiqh, this establishes the principle that animals fed on impure substances require a purification period before consumption, with durations varying by species size and metabolic rate. This ruling highlights the practical application of dietary purity (taharah) in daily life, ensuring that meat is not only ritually slaughtered but also physically pure.
